question: Identify the root cause of the network fault: which device, what changed, and why it breaks.
description: R2 moves both OSPF process 100 interfaces from area 0 to area 1 while R0 keeps the shared R0-R2 link in area 0. The area mismatch prevents the adjacency from remaining FULL, so neither router learns the other router's Loopback0 route. The independent direct-iBGP R3-R4 pair remains unchanged.
expected_rca: Root cause: on 100.64.0.102 (R2), OSPF process 100 was changed so Loopback0 and GigabitEthernet0/0/0/3 belong to area 1 instead of area 0, while R0 keeps its side of the shared link in area 0. The two link endpoints therefore advertise different OSPF area IDs and cannot maintain an adjacency, so R0 and R2 stop exchanging their Loopback0 routes. Fix: move R2's Loopback0 and GigabitEthernet0/0/0/3 assignments back to OSPF area 0.
expected_symptoms: RP/0/RP0/CPU0:Sep  8 18:59:50.863 UTC: ospf[1035]: %ROUTING-OSPF-5-ADJCHG : Process 100, Nbr 192.0.2.2 on GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1 in area 0 from FULL to DOWN, Neighbor Down: dead timer expired, vrf default vrfid 0x60000000

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:Sep  8 18:59:11.550 UTC: ospf[1035]: %ROUTING-OSPF-5-ADJCHG : Process 100, Nbr 192.0.2.0 on GigabitEthernet0/0/0/3 in area 0 from FULL to DOWN, Neighbor Down: interface down or detached, vrf default vrfid 0x60000000

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:Sep  8 18:59:14.125 UTC: ospf[1035]: %ROUTING-OSPF-4-ERRRCV : Received invalid packet: mismatch area ID, from backbone area must be virtual-link but not found from 192.0.0.1, GigabitEthernet0/0/0/3

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:Sep  8 18:59:32.921 UTC: ospf[1035]: %ROUTING-OSPF-4-ERRRCV : Received invalid packet: mismatch area ID, from backbone area must be virtual-link but not found from 192.0.0.1, GigabitEthernet0/0/0/3

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:Sep  8 18:59:51.920 UTC: ospf[1035]: %ROUTING-OSPF-4-ERRRCV : Received invalid packet: mismatch area ID, from backbone area must be virtual-link but not found from 192.0.0.1, GigabitEthernet0/0/0/3
expected_symptoms_summary:
OSPF adjacency state change (%ROUTING-OSPF-5-ADJCHG):
- R0: neighbor 192.0.2.2 on GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1 (area 0) FULL → DOWN reason "dead timer expired".
- R2: neighbor 192.0.2.0 on GigabitEthernet0/0/0/3 (area 0) FULL → DOWN reason "interface down or detached".
- Bilateral: both ends (R0, R2) report the transition.

OSPF packet receive error (%ROUTING-OSPF-4-ERRRCV):
- R2: mismatch area ID from peer 192.0.0.1 on GigabitEthernet0/0/0/3.
- R2: mismatch area ID from peer 192.0.0.1 on GigabitEthernet0/0/0/3.
- R2: mismatch area ID from peer 192.0.0.1 on GigabitEthernet0/0/0/3.
expected_state_diffs: R2 `show running-config router ospf 100`: Loopback0 and GigabitEthernet0/0/0/3 are under area 1 (baseline: both are under area 0).
R0/R2 `show ospf neighbor detail`: the R0-R2 adjacency is not FULL after the mutation (baseline: FULL).
R0 `show route ipv4 unicast 192.0.2.2/32`: the R2 Loopback0 OSPF route is absent after the mutation (baseline: present).
R2 `show route ipv4 unicast 192.0.2.0/32`: the R0 Loopback0 OSPF route is absent after the mutation (baseline: present).
R3/R4 `show bgp ipv4 unicast summary`: the independent direct-iBGP session remains Established, and R4 retains the BGP route for 192.0.2.3/32.

apply.commands:
configure terminal
router ospf 100
 no area 0
 area 1
  interface Loopback0
   passive enable
  interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/3
